title: FlexLine Account Lifecycle: End of the Draw Period, Closing, Charge-Off and Reporting
content:
A line under FlexLine Personal Lines of Credit leaves the draw period, closes or is charged off on the terms below.

## Clauses in force

- **Closing at the borrower's request.** A borrower may close the line at any time: with a 0.00 balance it closes immediately, and with a balance it is closed to new draws and moves to repayment at once, then closes when repaid.
- **Repaid lines.** A line in repayment closes as repaid after the draw period when its balance reaches 0.00.
- **Charge-off.** A line is charged off once the current date is at least the charge-off days past due after the oldest unpaid due date. Days past due are counted in calendar days starting the day after the oldest unpaid due date. The oldest unpaid due date is the one Larkspur's record of the line shows as its next due date.
- **Credit reporting.** Delinquency is reported once a line reaches the tier's delinquency-reporting days past due.
- **Declined applications.** A declined application leaves no line.

## Clause no longer in force

The following clause is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis:

> When the draw period ends the line moves to repayment and the balance is repaid in level payments over the tier's repayment period at the APR in force.

## How a line closes

| Situation | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Borrower closes, balance 0.00 | closed immediately, at the borrower's request with a zero balance |
| Borrower closes, balance above 0.00 | closed to new draws and in repayment at once; closes when repaid |
| Line in repayment, balance reaches 0.00 | closed as repaid after the draw period |

## Charge-off boundary (abstract cases, 180 days)

The comparison is "at least", so the boundary day itself qualifies.

| Current date | Days past due | Charged off |
|---|---|---|
| oldest unpaid due date plus 179 days | 179 | No |
| oldest unpaid due date plus 180 days | 180 | Yes |
